runner.invocation: interactive Automotive E/E Evidence batch-02 primary-source verification

grouping_resolution.note: Single item-level primary source; no grouping ambiguity.

sources.title: COVESA’s Hidden Gem: The vSomeIP Project
sources.role: Official COVESA project article used to verify project scope, relationship to SOME/IP/VSS and project history.

claims.text: COVESA states that the vSomeIP stack implements the SOME/IP protocol and provides a communication mechanism for exchanging structured vehicle data.
claims.context: Project identity and implementation scope on the official host page.

claims.text: COVESA states that BMW Group initially contributed the vSomeIP code and that COVESA has hosted the project since the GENIVI era.
COVESA presents VSS as a common vehicle-data model and vSomeIP as a complementary communication mechanism.
claims.context: Consortium architectural framing, not a normative interoperability guarantee.

limitations.text: The same page makes broad adoption/deployment statements; this card does not treat those as independently verified production-deployment evidence.

targets.target: Verify the official scope/status and architecture-significant statements on covesa-vsomeip; distinguish directly checkable facts from organization/project claims.
targets.finding: The official COVESA page establishes vSomeIP project scope, SOME/IP implementation role and its relationship to VSS; adoption scale is deliberately not upgraded to an independent fact.

editorial.why_now_note: A concrete open SOME/IP middleware implementation is directly relevant to the service-oriented runtime layer of centralized/zonal E/E architectures.
editorial.rationale: Provides implementation-level evidence that complements protocol/specification discussion without equating project-host claims with independent adoption proof.
